items.title: ‘Haaland must be worried’: Thierno Barry’s rise has David Moyes purring
items.summary: Everton striker has worked hard to find his scoring touch after admitting he hit ‘rock bottom’ at times last season A most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. The rise of Thierno Barry may have surprised even the man himself but stands as a fitting reward for single-minded perseverance and the refusal to quit. “Fabulous” was David Moyes’s take on Barry’s last performance for Everton, when a double against Coventry took the striker to 10 goals for the season in all competitions and his team temporarily up to fifth. It was high praise indeed from a manager who does not dispense tributes freely, and can appear to be on the French forward’s case constantly, but was no more than Barry deserved for a display that also featured an assist for Everton’s third goal of the night. His six Premier League goals leave him joint third alongside Evanilson of Bournemouth and Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson. Continue reading...

items.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
items.summary: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson Match report: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision Continue reading...
